attributes.description: Foreign key linking to biostatistics.statistical_endpoint. Business justification: Sample size calculations are performed for specific statistical endpoints — the primary endpoint drives the power calculation, and secondary endpoints may have their own calculations. Linking sample_s
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study for which this sample size calculation was performed.
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: accrual_period_months
attributes.description: The assumed patient accrual (enrollment) period in months, used in time-to-event sample size calculations to determine the number of events required.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: allocation_ratio
attributes.description: The randomization allocation ratio between treatment arms (e.g., '1:1', '2:1', '1:1:1'), specifying the relative number of subjects assigned to each arm.
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM Randomization Standards

attributes.name: alpha_level
attributes.description: The pre-specified Type I error rate (significance level, alpha) used in the sample size calculation, typically 0.05 for two-sided or 0.025 for one-sided tests.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance; EMA Guideline on Multiplicity

attributes.name: alpha_spending_method
attributes.description: The alpha-spending function applied to control Type I error across planned interim analyses (e.g., O'Brien-Fleming, Pocock, Lan-DeMets). Null or 'none' if no interim analysis is planned.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Adaptive Design Guidance; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: amendment_reason
attributes.description: Narrative justification for revising a prior version of the sample size calculation, such as updated assumptions from interim data, protocol amendment, or regulatory feedback.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Protocol Amendment Guidance; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the sample size calculation was formally approved by the responsible biostatistician, marking readiness for inclusion in regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: calc_date
attributes.description: The date on which this sample size calculation was performed or finalized, serving as the principal business event date for regulatory traceability.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: calc_identifier
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code or reference number assigned to this sample size calculation, used in regulatory submissions and protocol documentation (e.g., SSC-2024-001).
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Sample Size Calculations

attributes.name: calc_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the sample size calculation record, from initial draft through regulatory approval to archival.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: calc_version
attributes.description: Version number of this sample size calculation (e.g., v1.0, v2.1), enabling tracking of revisions driven by protocol amendments or updated assumptions.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this sample size calculation record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: dropout_rate
attributes.description: The assumed proportion of enrolled subjects expected to discontinue or be lost to follow-up, used to inflate the calculated sample size to ensure adequate evaluable subjects.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Missing Data in Clinical Trials

attributes.name: effect_size
attributes.description: The clinically meaningful difference or effect size assumed between treatment arms (e.g., mean difference, odds ratio, hazard ratio) used as the basis for the sample size calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Sample Size Calculations

attributes.name: effect_size_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the assumed effect size (e.g., mmHg, %, hazard ratio, odds ratio, mean difference), providing dimensional context for regulatory interpretation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM Unit Standards

attributes.name: event_rate_control
attributes.description: The assumed event rate or response rate in the control arm, applicable for binary or time-to-event endpoints. Null for continuous endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: event_rate_treatment
attributes.description: The assumed event rate or response rate in the treatment arm, applicable for binary or time-to-event endpoints. Null for continuous endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: follow_up_period_months
attributes.description: The assumed minimum follow-up period in months after the last patient enrolled, used in time-to-event calculations to ensure sufficient events are observed.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Oncology Endpoint Guidance

attributes.name: hypothesis_type
attributes.description: The statistical hypothesis framework applied (superiority, non-inferiority, equivalence), which determines the directionality and margin used in the sample size formula.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E10 Choice of Control Group; FDA Non-Inferiority Guidance

attributes.name: interim_analysis_planned
attributes.description: Indicates whether one or more interim analyses are planned for this study, which may require alpha-spending adjustments to the sample size calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Adaptive Design Guidance; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: median_survival_control
attributes.description: The assumed median survival time in the control arm for time-to-event endpoints, used in log-rank or exponential model-based sample size calculations. Null for non-survival endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Oncology Endpoint Guidance

attributes.name: non_inferiority_margin
attributes.description: The pre-specified non-inferiority or equivalence margin (delta) used in the hypothesis test, applicable when hypothesis_type is non_inferiority or equivalence. Null for superiority designs.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E10; FDA Non-Inferiority Guidance 2016

attributes.name: number_of_arms
attributes.description: Total number of treatment arms (including control) in the study design, used to determine the allocation structure and multiplicity adjustments.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E10

attributes.name: number_of_events_required
attributes.description: The minimum number of primary endpoint events (e.g., deaths, progressions) required to achieve the specified power for time-to-event analyses. Null for non-event-driven endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Oncology Endpoint Guidance; EMA Guideline on Survival Analysis

attributes.name: power
attributes.description: The pre-specified statistical power (1 minus Type II error rate, beta) used in the calculation, representing the probability of detecting the assumed effect size. Typically 0.80 or 0.90.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: primary_endpoint_type
attributes.description: Statistical nature of the primary efficacy endpoint (e.g., continuous, binary, time-to-event, ordinal, count) that drives the choice of sample size formula.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E9(R1) Estimands Addendum; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: reference_source
attributes.description: Citation or reference for the data source used to derive the assumed effect size, standard deviation, or event rate (e.g., published literature citation, prior Phase II study identifier, internal pilot data).
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: sample_size_per_arm
attributes.description: The calculated number of subjects required per treatment arm to achieve the specified power at the given alpha level, accounting for the assumed effect size and standard deviation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: software_name
attributes.description: Name of the validated statistical software used to perform the sample size calculation (e.g., PASS, nQuery Advisor, SAS PROC POWER, R), required for regulatory audit trail.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E9; CDISC Validation Standards

attributes.name: software_version
attributes.description: Version number of the statistical software used (e.g., PASS 2023, nQuery 9.1), required for reproducibility and regulatory validation documentation.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 820 (software validation)

attributes.name: standard_deviation
attributes.description: The assumed population standard deviation for continuous endpoints, derived from prior studies or literature, used in the sample size formula. Null for non-continuous endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: statistical_method
attributes.description: The specific statistical formula or method used for the calculation (e.g., two-sample t-test, log-rank test, chi-square test, Kaplan-Meier), providing methodological traceability.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: study_design_type
attributes.description: The clinical trial design type (e.g., parallel group, crossover, factorial, adaptive) that determines the statistical methodology applied in the sample size calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance

attributes.name: study_phase
attributes.description: Clinical development phase of the study (Phase I through Phase IV) for which the sample size is being calculated, influencing regulatory expectations and statistical rigor.
attributes.value_regex: Phase I|Phase II|Phase IIa|Phase IIb|Phase III|Phase IV
attributes.references: ICH E8 General Considerations for Clinical Trials; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: test_sidedness
attributes.description: Specifies whether the statistical test is one-sided or two-sided, directly affecting the critical value and resulting sample size.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: total_enrollment_target
attributes.description: The total number of subjects to be enrolled (randomized) after inflating the total sample size by the assumed dropout rate, representing the actual recruitment target submitted in the protocol.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: total_sample_size
attributes.description: The total number of subjects required across all treatment arms before applying the dropout inflation, representing the minimum evaluable sample.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this sample size calculation record was most recently modified, supporting version control and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2)

products.name: adam_dataset_spec
products.description: Specification record for each ADaM (Analysis Data Model) dataset produced for a study, including variable-level detail. Captures dataset name (e.g., ADSL, ADAE, ADTTE, ADLB), dataset class (ADSL, BDS, OCCDS, OTHER), purpose, key variables with derivation algorithms, variable types, lengths, controlled terminology references, CDISC ADaM core designations (Required/Expected/Permissible), source SDTM domains, programming language, SAS program reference, and approval status. SSOT for ADaM dataset and variable design consumed by SAS programmers.
products.reference: ADaM Dataset Specification — CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide

attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study for which this ADaM dataset specification is authored. Links the specification to its parent protocol and study context.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: ADaM datasets are submitted to FDA/EMA as CDISC-required components of NDA/BLA/MAA submissions. The submission_flag attribute on adam_dataset_spec confirms this business reality. Direct FK supports su

attributes.name: adam_ig_version
attributes.description: Version of the CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide to which this dataset specification conforms (e.g., 'ADaM IG v1.3', 'ADSL v1.1', 'BDS v1.1'). Required for regulatory submission conformance validation.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA Data Standards

attributes.name: analysis_variable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this variable is a primary analysis variable (AVAL, AVALC, or equivalent) used directly in statistical analyses and TLF production. True = analysis variable; False = supporting/descriptive variable. Guides programmer prioritization.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3; ICH E9 Statistical Principles

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which this ADaM dataset specification was formally approved by the lead biostatistician and/or statistical programming lead. Marks the specification as ready for SAS programming implementation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: authored_by
attributes.description: Name or user identifier of the biostatistician who authored this ADaM dataset specification. Establishes accountability and is referenced in the audit trail for regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: blinding_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether this ADaM dataset contains unblinded treatment assignment data. Blinded = treatment codes masked; Unblinded = actual treatment assignments visible (post-DBL or for open-label studies); Open-Label = study design is inherently unblinded. Governs access control and data release procedures.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: change_reason
attributes.description: Narrative justification for changes introduced in this version of the specification relative to the prior version (e.g., 'SAP amendment v2.0 added new secondary endpoint', 'Protocol amendment PA-003 added new visit'). Required for change control documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: codelist_name
attributes.description: Name of the specific CDISC or sponsor-defined codelist associated with this variable (e.g., 'NY', 'SEX', 'RACE', 'DTYPE'). Referenced in the define.xml ItemDef and used for PINNACLE 21 conformance validation.
attributes.references: CDISC Controlled Terminology; CDISC Define-XML v2.1; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: controlled_terminology
attributes.description: Reference to the controlled terminology codelist applicable to this variable (e.g., 'CDISC SDTM CT RACE', 'NCI Thesaurus C66742', 'MedDRA v26.0 PT', 'WHO-DD'). Ensures standardized values for regulatory submission and cross-study comparability.
attributes.references: CDISC Controlled Terminology; NCI Thesaurus; MedDRA; WHO-DD; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: core_designation
attributes.description: CDISC ADaM core designation indicating the requirement level for this variable. Required = must be present in all datasets of this class; Expected = should be present when applicable; Permissible = may be included at sponsor discretion. Drives conformance validation.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this ADaM dataset specification record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and record lineage per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

attributes.name: dataset_class
attributes.description: CDISC ADaM structural class of the dataset. ADSL = Subject-Level Analysis Dataset (one record per subject); BDS = Basic Data Structure (one or more records per subject per analysis parameter per analysis timepoint); OCCDS = Occurrence Data Structure (one or more records per subject per occurrence of an event); OTHER = datasets not conforming to a standard class.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3

attributes.name: dataset_label
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive label for the dataset (e.g., 'Subject-Level Analysis Dataset', 'Adverse Events Analysis Dataset'). Used in SAS PROC CONTENTS output and regulatory submission metadata.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: dataset_name
attributes.description: Short, uppercase dataset name conforming to CDISC ADaM naming conventions (e.g., ADSL, ADAE, ADTTE, ADLB, ADCM, ADEX, ADRS). Maximum 8 characters per CDISC standard. This is the externally-known identifier used by SAS programmers and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: dataset_purpose
attributes.description: Narrative description of the analytical purpose of this dataset, including the primary analysis populations it supports, key endpoints addressed, and its role in the Clinical Study Report (CSR). Authored by the biostatistician.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3; ICH E3 Structure of CSR

attributes.name: define_xml_version
attributes.description: Version of the CDISC Define-XML standard used to generate the define.xml metadata file for this dataset (e.g., 'Define-XML v2.0', 'Define-XML v2.1'). Required for FDA and EMA electronic submission packages.
attributes.references: CDISC Define-XML v2.1; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA Data Standards

attributes.name: derivation_algorithm
attributes.description: Detailed narrative or pseudocode describing the derivation logic for this variable, including source variables, transformation rules, imputation methods (e.g., LOCF), and conditional logic. The primary programming instruction for SAS programmers. Must be unambiguous and traceable to the SAP.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3; ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC ADaM Traceability

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this version of the ADaM dataset specification is effective and authoritative for programming use. For superseded versions, this marks the start of the version's validity period.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: interim_analysis_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dataset specification is intended for use in an interim analysis (True) or the final analysis (False). Interim analysis datasets may have restricted access and require DSMB/DMC review procedures.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; FDA Adaptive Design Guidance

attributes.name: key_variables
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of variable names that form the unique record key for this dataset (e.g., 'USUBJID' for ADSL; 'USUBJID, PARAMCD, ADT' for BDS datasets). Defines the grain of the dataset and is critical for merge/join operations in SAS programming.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3

attributes.name: pinnacle21_validation_status
attributes.description: Result of the Pinnacle 21 (formerly OpenCDISC) conformance validation run against this ADaM dataset. Pass = no errors; Pass with Warnings = minor issues noted; Fail = conformance errors requiring remediation; Not Run = validation pending. Required for FDA submission readiness.
attributes.references: FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; Pinnacle 21 Enterprise

attributes.name: programming_language
attributes.description: Statistical programming language used to implement this ADaM dataset specification. SAS is the regulatory standard; R and Python may be used for exploratory or supplemental analyses. Governs QC and validation approach.
attributes.references: FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; SAS Drug Development

attributes.name: qc_method
attributes.description: Quality control methodology applied to validate this ADaM dataset. Double Programming = independent programmer recreates dataset and compares; Peer Review = senior programmer reviews code and output; Independent QC = separate QC team validates; Not Required = exploratory/non-submission dataset.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: qc_status
attributes.description: Current QC completion status for this ADaM dataset. Not Started = QC not yet initiated; In Progress = QC underway; QC Complete = dataset passed QC validation; Failed QC = discrepancies found requiring programmer remediation.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; ICH E6(R2) GCP; SAS Drug Development

attributes.name: sas_format
attributes.description: SAS display format assigned to this variable (e.g., 'DATE9.', 'DATETIME20.', '$CHAR200.', '8.2'). Governs how values are displayed in SAS output and define.xml DisplayFormat attribute. Required for SAS Drug Development programming specifications.
attributes.references: SAS Drug Development Standards; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3

attributes.name: sas_informat
attributes.description: SAS informat used to read raw values into this variable (e.g., 'YYMMDD10.', 'E8601DT.', '$CHAR200.'). Required for date/datetime variables derived from ISO 8601 SDTM character dates. Specified in SAS Drug Development programming specs.
attributes.references: SAS Drug Development Standards; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3

attributes.name: sas_program_reference
attributes.description: File path or program name of the SAS program in SAS Drug Development that produces this ADaM dataset (e.g., '/studies/STUDY001/adam/programs/adsl.sas'). Links the specification to its implementing program for traceability and QC.
attributes.references: SAS Drug Development; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: source_variable
attributes.description: Name of the source SDTM or predecessor ADaM variable(s) from which this variable is derived (e.g., 'AE.AEDECOD', 'DM.RFSTDTC', 'ADSL.TRT01P'). Supports CDISC traceability requirements and audit trail for regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Traceability; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: spec_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the ADaM dataset specification. Draft = initial authoring; Under Review = submitted for biostatistics/programming review; Approved = formally signed off for programming use; Superseded = replaced by a newer version; Retired = no longer applicable.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: spec_version
attributes.description: Version number of this ADaM dataset specification document following major.minor versioning (e.g., 1.0, 1.1, 2.0). Incremented upon each approved revision to support change control and audit traceability.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: submission_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this ADaM dataset is included in the regulatory submission package (NDA, BLA, MAA, or IND). True = included in eCTD submission; False = internal analysis only. Governs define.xml inclusion and FDA/EMA conformance validation requirements.
attributes.references: FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA Data Standards; ICH M4 CTD; 21 CFR Part 314

attributes.name: superseded_date
attributes.description: Date on which this version of the specification was superseded by a newer version. Null for the current active version. Supports version history and audit trail for regulatory inspection.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: timing_variable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this variable is a CDISC ADaM timing variable (e.g., ADT, ADTM, ADY, AVISIT, AVISITN). True = timing variable subject to ADaM timing variable conventions. Used for conformance checking and define.xml classification.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this ADaM dataset specification record. Supports change tracking and audit trail per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

attributes.name: variable_label
attributes.description: Descriptive SAS variable label (max 256 characters) providing a human-readable description of the variable (e.g., 'Unique Subject Identifier', 'Parameter Code', 'Analysis Value'). Appears in SAS PROC CONTENTS and submission define.xml.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: variable_length
attributes.description: SAS variable length in bytes. For character variables, specifies maximum string length (e.g., 200 for USUBJID). For numeric variables, typically 8 (SAS default double precision). Required for SAS dataset creation and define.xml generation.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3; SAS Drug Development Standards

attributes.name: variable_name
attributes.description: SAS-compliant variable name for this specification record (uppercase, max 8 characters per SAS/CDISC convention, e.g., USUBJID, PARAMCD, AVAL, DTYPE). Each row in this table represents one variable within the dataset specification.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3; SAS Drug Development Standards

attributes.name: variable_type
attributes.description: SAS data type of the variable. Char = character/string variable; Num = numeric variable. Governs SAS dataset structure and informat/format assignments in programming specifications.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3; SAS Drug Development Standards

products.name: adam_variable_spec

Enables automated SAS program generation and reviewer validation.

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study for which this ADaM variable specification is defined. Scopes the variable spec to a specific protocol.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice

attributes.name: adam_structure
attributes.description: CDISC ADaM structural classification of the parent dataset: ADSL (Subject-Level Analysis Dataset), BDS (Basic Data Structure — one record per subject per parameter per analysis timepoint), OCCDS (Occurrence Data Structure — for events like AEs and CMs), or OTHER.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the variable specification was formally approved by the responsible biostatistician or lead programmer. Marks the transition from draft to approved status in the specification lifecycle.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: baseline_flag
attributes.description: Name of the associated baseline flag variable (e.g., ABLFL) used to identify the baseline record for this analysis variable. Supports change-from-baseline derivations and is required for BDS datasets.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM BDS Implementation Guide

attributes.name: change_from_baseline_var
attributes.description: Name of the corresponding change-from-baseline variable (CHG) or percent change-from-baseline variable (PCHG) derived from this analysis variable. Establishes the analytical linkage between AVAL and its change metrics.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM BDS Implementation Guide

attributes.name: codelist_name
attributes.description: Name of the specific CDISC controlled terminology codelist associated with this variable (e.g., NY, DTYPE, PARAMCD, AVISIT). Used in DEFINE-XML generation and submission package validation.
attributes.references: CDISC Controlled Terminology; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, clarifications, or reviewer comments regarding the variable specification. May include sponsor-specific guidance, open questions, or cross-references to SAP sections.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: controlled_terminology_ref
attributes.description: Reference to the applicable CDISC controlled terminology codelist, MedDRA dictionary, WHO-DD, or CTCAE version governing the permissible values for this variable. Example: 'CDISC CT DTYPE 2023-09-29', 'MedDRA v26.0 PT', 'CTCAE v5.0'.
attributes.references: CDISC Controlled Terminology; MedDRA; WHO-DD; CTCAE; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: core_designation
attributes.description: CDISC ADaM core classification indicating the mandatory status of the variable: Required (must be present), Expected (should be present unless not applicable), Permissible (optional, may be included), or Conditionally Required (required when specific conditions are met). Drives compliance validation.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this variable specification record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: define_xml_display_format
attributes.description: Display format specification for this variable as it will appear in the DEFINE-XML submission metadata file (define.xml). Includes display format string and any associated decode mapping for coded values. Required for FDA/EMA electronic submission packages.
attributes.references: CDISC Define-XML v2.1; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA Data Standards

attributes.name: derivation_algorithm
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the derivation logic used to compute or assign the variable's value. Includes source variable references, transformation rules, imputation methods (e.g., LOCF), and conditional logic. Enables automated SAS program generation and independent QC programmer validation.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; ICH E9 Statistical Principles

attributes.name: format_name
attributes.description: SAS format or informat name applied to this variable for display or input purposes (e.g., DATE9., DATETIME20., $CHAR200.). Used in SAS program generation and dataset creation.
attributes.references: SAS Drug Development; SAS Language Reference

attributes.name: imputation_method
attributes.description: Description of the missing data imputation method applied to this variable as specified in the SAP. Examples: LOCF (Last Observation Carried Forward), BOCF (Baseline Observation Carried Forward), multiple imputation, worst-case, or none. Critical for regulatory submission transparency.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands; FDA Guidance on Missing Data; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: is_analysis_variable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this variable is designated as a primary or secondary analysis variable (AVAL, AVALC, or equivalent) used directly in statistical analyses as defined in the SAP.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; ICH E9 Statistical Principles

attributes.name: is_key_variable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this variable is part of the dataset's sort key (BY variables) as defined in the ADaM dataset specification. Key variables determine dataset sort order and are required for PROC SORT and merge operations in SAS.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: is_param_variable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this variable is a PARAM/PARAMCD/PARAMN grouping variable used in BDS (Basic Data Structure) or OCCDS datasets to identify the analysis parameter. Drives parameter-level filtering in TLF production.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM BDS Implementation Guide

attributes.name: origin
attributes.description: CDISC-defined origin classification indicating how the variable value is obtained: Derived (computed from other variables), Assigned (set by sponsor/programmer per protocol), Collected (directly from eCRF/EDC), Protocol (defined in study protocol), or Not Available.
attributes.references: CDISC Define-XML v2.1; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: population_flag
attributes.description: Name of the analysis population flag variable this specification defines (e.g., ITTFL for Intent-to-Treat, SAFFL for Safety, PPROTFL for Per Protocol, FASFL for Full Analysis Set). Null if the variable is not a population flag.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; ICH E9 Statistical Principles

attributes.name: predecessor_variable
attributes.description: Name of the predecessor variable from which this variable is directly derived, as required in DEFINE-XML metadata. Establishes the data lineage chain from SDTM collected data through ADaM derived variables for regulatory traceability.
attributes.references: CDISC Define-XML v2.1; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: qc_date
attributes.description: Date on which the independent QC programmer completed verification of this variable's derivation. Recorded as part of the audit trail for regulatory submission readiness.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: qc_programmer
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the independent QC programmer responsible for verifying the derivation of this variable through independent programming. Required for dual-programming QC methodology compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: qc_status
attributes.description: Current QC lifecycle status of this variable specification. Tracks progression from initial draft through independent QC programmer review to final approval. QC Passed indicates the derivation has been independently verified by a second programmer. Locked indicates the spec is frozen for DBL.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: sas_program_reference
attributes.description: Name or path of the SAS program in SAS Drug Development that implements the derivation for this variable. Enables direct linkage between the variable specification and its executable SAS code for QC and audit purposes.
attributes.references: SAS Drug Development; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: significant_digits
attributes.description: Number of significant digits to retain for numeric variables in analysis outputs and TLF displays. Defined in the SAP and applied during SAS program generation to ensure consistent rounding across tables, listings, and figures.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: source_dataset
attributes.description: Primary SDTM or ADaM source dataset from which this variable is derived or mapped (e.g., AE, LB, VS, ADSL). Supports traceability from analysis results back to raw clinical data.
attributes.references: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: source_variables
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of source variable names (from SDTM datasets or other ADaM datasets) used in the derivation of this variable. Supports data lineage tracing and ALCOA+ compliance. Example: 'SDTM.AE.AESTDTC, SDTM.DM.RFSTDTC'.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: spec_status
attributes.description: Lifecycle status of this variable specification document. Draft indicates work in progress; In Review indicates under biostatistician or sponsor review; Approved indicates finalized and signed off; Superseded indicates replaced by a newer version; Retired indicates no longer applicable.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: spec_version
attributes.description: Version identifier for this variable specification record, following semantic versioning (e.g., v1.0, v1.1, v2.0). Incremented when derivation algorithm, source variables, or controlled terminology references are updated. Supports audit trail and change management.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: therapeutic_area
attributes.description: Therapeutic area or disease indication for which this variable specification is designed (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Neurology). Relevant for CDISC Therapeutic Area User Guides (TAUGs) compliance and cross-study reuse.
attributes.references: CDISC Therapeutic Area User Guides (TAUGs); FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this variable specification record. Required for change tracking and audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: variable_label
attributes.description: Human-readable SAS variable label (up to 40 characters) describing the variable's business meaning. Used in SAS output headers, TLF footnotes, and reviewer documentation. Example: 'Analysis Value', 'Parameter Code'.

attributes.name: actual_analysis_date
attributes.description: The actual calendar date on which the interim analysis was executed and results were produced. May differ from planned date due to enrollment pace or operational factors.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: adam_dataset_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the CDISC ADaM datasets used as input to this interim analysis, ensuring traceability between the analysis results and the underlying data snapshot.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; FDA Data Standards Catalog; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: adaptation_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of any pre-specified design adaptation implemented as a result of this interim analysis (e.g., sample size re-estimation, dose selection, population enrichment). Populated only when analysis_outcome is 'adapt'.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: alpha_allocated
attributes.description: The portion of the overall one-sided or two-sided alpha (Type I error rate) allocated to this specific interim look by the alpha spending function. Used to derive the efficacy stopping boundary.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: alpha_spending_function
attributes.description: The pre-specified alpha spending function used to allocate the overall Type I error rate across interim looks, as defined in the SAP. Common functions include O'Brien-Fleming, Pocock, Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming approximation, Lan-DeMets Pocock approximation, Hwang-Shih-DeCani, or a custom function.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); Lan & DeMets (1983); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: alpha_spending_parameter
attributes.description: Numeric parameter (gamma) for the selected alpha spending function, where applicable (e.g., the gamma parameter for Hwang-Shih-DeCani function). Null for functions that do not require a parameter.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); Hwang, Shih & DeCani (1990)

attributes.name: analysis_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for this interim analysis, used in regulatory submissions, DSMB/DMC charters, and TMF documentation (e.g., IA-STUDY001-001).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: analysis_number
attributes.description: Sequential ordinal number identifying this interim analysis within the study (e.g., 1 for first interim, 2 for second interim). Used to track the series of planned looks at accumulating data.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: analysis_outcome
attributes.description: The formal decision or recommendation resulting from the interim analysis: continue (study proceeds as planned), stop_efficacy (early termination for demonstrated benefit), stop_futility (early termination for lack of benefit), stop_safety (early termination for safety concerns), adapt (pre-specified design adaptation implemented), or pending (DSMB/DMC recommendation not yet issued).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: analysis_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the interim analysis: planned (scheduled but not yet initiated), in_progress (analysis underway), completed (results finalized), cancelled (analysis removed from plan), or on_hold (temporarily suspended).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: analysis_type
attributes.description: Classification of the interim analysis by its primary statistical purpose: efficacy (test for early stopping due to benefit), futility (test for early stopping due to lack of benefit), safety (review of accumulating safety data), adaptive (pre-specified adaptation of design parameters), combined_efficacy_futility, or administrative (data review without hypothesis testing). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: efficacy|futility|safety|adaptive|combined_efficacy_futility|administrative — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: conditional_power
attributes.description: Probability of achieving a statistically significant result at the final analysis, conditional on the data observed at this interim look and assuming the originally hypothesized treatment effect. Used in futility assessments.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019; Lan & Wittes (1988)

attributes.name: confidentiality_level
attributes.description: Data classification level assigned to the interim analysis results and associated outputs, controlling access and distribution. Interim analysis results are typically restricted to prevent unblinding of the broader study team.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019; GDPR; HIPAA; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this interim analysis record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: data_cutoff_date
attributes.description: The date through which subject data was included in the interim analysis dataset. All data collected after this date is excluded from the analysis. Critical for regulatory traceability and blinding integrity.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Data

attributes.name: dsmb_involved
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) / Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) Involvement Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) reviewed the unblinded interim analysis results (True = DSMB/DMC reviewed; False = internal review only).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on DMCs 2006; EMA Guideline on DMCs

attributes.name: dsmb_meeting_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) convened to review the interim analysis results and issue a recommendation.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance on DMCs 2006; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: efficacy_boundary_value
attributes.description: Pre-specified critical value (e.g., z-statistic or p-value threshold) for the efficacy stopping boundary at this interim look. If the observed test statistic exceeds this boundary, early stopping for efficacy is triggered.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); O'Brien & Fleming (1979); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: events_observed
attributes.description: Number of primary endpoint events (e.g., deaths, disease progression events) observed as of the data cutoff date. Applicable for event-driven trials; used to compute the actual information fraction.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM ADTTE; FDA Oncology Guidance

attributes.name: events_planned_total
attributes.description: Total number of primary endpoint events required for the final analysis as specified in the SAP and sample size calculation. Used as the denominator for the information fraction in event-driven trials.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: firewall_maintained
attributes.description: Indicates whether a blinding firewall was maintained between the unblinded interim analysis team and the blinded study team (True = firewall in place; False = firewall not maintained or not applicable). Critical for regulatory compliance in adaptive trials.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: futility_boundary_binding
attributes.description: Indicates whether the futility stopping boundary is binding (True = mandatory stop if crossed; False = non-binding/advisory only). Binding futility boundaries affect the overall Type I error calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: futility_boundary_value
attributes.description: Pre-specified critical value for the futility stopping boundary at this interim look. If the observed test statistic falls below this boundary, early stopping for futility (lack of efficacy) may be triggered. May be binding or non-binding per the SAP.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: information_fraction_actual
attributes.description: Observed proportion of total planned statistical information actually accumulated at the time of this interim analysis. May differ from planned fraction due to enrollment variability or event rate changes.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); Lan-DeMets alpha spending framework

attributes.name: information_fraction_planned
attributes.description: Pre-specified proportion of the total planned statistical information (e.g., events, subjects) accumulated at the time of this interim analysis, expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1 (e.g., 0.5000 = 50% of planned events). Drives alpha spending calculations.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); Lan-DeMets alpha spending framework; FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing additional context, operational notes, deviations from the pre-specified plan, or DSMB/DMC commentary relevant to this interim analysis that is not captured in structured fields.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: observed_p_value
attributes.description: The nominal p-value from the primary hypothesis test at this interim analysis. Must be interpreted in the context of the alpha spending boundary, not as a standalone significance threshold.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: observed_test_statistic
attributes.description: The actual computed test statistic (e.g., z-score, chi-square, log-rank statistic) from the interim analysis dataset. Compared against efficacy and futility boundaries to determine the outcome.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; SAS Drug Development

attributes.name: planned_analysis_date
attributes.description: Pre-specified calendar date on which the interim analysis is planned to be conducted, as documented in the SAP and DSMB/DMC charter.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the interim analysis results or the resulting design adaptation must be submitted to a regulatory authority (FDA, EMA, PMDA, etc.) as part of an IND, NDA, BLA, or MAA amendment (True = submission required; False = not required).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312; FDA IND Regulations; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E9(R1)

attributes.name: results_disclosed_externally
attributes.description: Indicates whether the interim analysis results have been disclosed externally (e.g., to regulators, in a public registry, or in a publication) prior to study completion (True = disclosed; False = not disclosed). Tracks blinding integrity at the study level.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); WHO ICTRP; EU CTR 536/2014; FDA Transparency Guidance

attributes.name: revised_sample_size
attributes.description: Updated total sample size determined through the pre-specified sample size re-estimation procedure at this interim analysis. Null if sample_size_reestimated is False.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: sample_size_reestimated
attributes.description: Indicates whether a pre-specified sample size re-estimation was performed as part of this interim analysis (True = sample size re-estimated; False = no re-estimation performed).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: sas_program_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the SAS Drug Development program or analysis package used to execute this interim analysis, enabling reproducibility and audit traceability.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC ADaM; SAS Drug Development platform

attributes.name: stopping_rule_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the specific stopping rule(s) triggered at this interim analysis, including the criterion crossed and the observed vs. boundary values. Populated only when stopping_rule_triggered is True.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: stopping_rule_triggered
attributes.description: Indicates whether any pre-specified stopping rule (efficacy, futility, or safety) was triggered by the results of this interim analysis (True = stopping rule crossed; False = no stopping rule triggered).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: subjects_enrolled_at_cutoff
attributes.description: Total number of subjects enrolled in the study as of the data cutoff date for this interim analysis. Provides context for the information fraction and statistical power.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC SDTM DM domain

attributes.name: unblinding_authorization_date
attributes.description: Date on which formal authorization was granted to unblind the interim analysis data, as documented in the unblinding log. Required for audit trail and blinding integrity compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: unblinding_scope
attributes.description: Defines the extent of treatment assignment unblinding performed for this interim analysis: full (all treatment assignments revealed to the analysis team), partial (only aggregate or summary-level unblinding), or none (blinded analysis only). Critical for blinding integrity management and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this interim analysis record was most recently modified, supporting audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: coding_complete

attributes.name: data_cut_date
attributes.description: The clinical data cut-off date defining which subject data and observations are included in this lock. All data with a collection date on or before this date is included in the locked dataset. Critical for interim and partial locks.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; ICH E9(R1) Addendum; CDISC ADaM Guidelines

attributes.name: dbl_event_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique identifier for this database lock event (e.g., DBL-2024-001). Used in regulatory submissions, TMF filings, and cross-system references in Medidata Rave and Oracle Siebel CTMS.

attributes.name: dm_approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which the Data Management representative provided electronic authorization for the database lock. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: dsmb_notification_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Notification Date
attributes.description: The date on which the DSMB/DMC was formally notified of the database lock and provided access to the locked dataset for their review.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on DSMB; ICH E9(R1)

attributes.name: dsmb_notification_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Notification Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) must be notified of this database lock event, typically for interim analysis locks where the DSMB reviews unblinded data.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on DSMB; ICH E9(R1)

attributes.name: lock_scope
attributes.description: Defines the scope of data included in this lock event. Full study locks the entire study database; interim locks a defined data cut for interim analysis; partial locks a subset of data (e.g., specific sites or forms); cohort locks a defined patient cohort; site-specific locks data from one or more named sites.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC Data Management Guidelines; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: lock_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the database lock event. Tracks progression from planning through execution and any subsequent unlock/re-lock cycles required for data corrections or amendments.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC Data Management Guidelines

attributes.name: lock_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time (with timezone) at which the database lock was executed in the EDC system (Medidata Rave). Required for 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail compliance and ALCOA+ data integrity standards.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles; CDISC Data Management Guidelines

attributes.name: lock_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the lock is a hard lock (no further data changes permitted without formal unlock and re-lock procedure) or a soft lock (data is locked for analysis but minor corrections may still be applied under controlled conditions). Hard locks are required prior to final DBL and regulatory submission.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC Data Management Guidelines

attributes.name: medical_monitor_approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which the Medical Monitor provided electronic authorization for the database lock. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: pre_lock_qc_completion_date

attributes.name: subjects_locked_count
attributes.description: Total number of study subjects whose data is included in this database lock event. Used for completeness verification and comparison against enrollment targets defined in the SAP.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC ADaM Guidelines

attributes.name: unblinding_date

attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

attributes.name: analysis_timepoint

attributes.name: confidence_interval_level
attributes.description: Pre-specified confidence interval level for the treatment effect estimate (e.g., 95.00 for a 95% CI, 97.50 for a one-sided 97.5% CI). Defined in the SAP and reported in TLFs and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials

attributes.name: covariates
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of pre-specified covariates and stratification factors included in the statistical model for this endpoint (e.g., 'baseline_value, region, age_group'). Defined in the SAP per EMA guideline on adjustment for baseline covariates.
attributes.references: EMA Guideline on Adjustment for Baseline Covariates; ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this statistical endpoint record was first created in the system. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: csr_section_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the Clinical Study Report (CSR) section where this endpoint's results are reported (e.g., 'Section 11.4.1'). Supports traceability from SAP endpoint definition to the final regulatory submission document per ICH E3.
attributes.references: ICH E3 Structure and Content of Clinical Study Reports; FDA CSR Guidance; EMA CSR Guidance

attributes.name: effect_measure
attributes.description: The statistical measure used to quantify the treatment effect for this endpoint (e.g., 'Mean Difference', 'Hazard Ratio', 'Odds Ratio', 'Risk Difference', 'Least Squares Mean Difference'). Specified in the SAP and reported in TLFs and the CSR.
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC ADaM; FDA Statistical Guidance; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials

attributes.name: endpoint_classification
attributes.description: Hierarchical classification of the endpoint within the study's inferential framework: primary (confirmatory, controls Type I error), secondary (supportive), exploratory (hypothesis-generating), or safety (adverse event-related). Drives multiplicity adjustment strategy.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Multiple Endpoints; EMA Guideline on Multiplicity Issues

attributes.name: endpoint_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the endpoint, used in SAP documents, TLF shells, and regulatory submissions. Follows the pattern EP-{STUDY_CODE}-{SEQ}.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM; ICH E9; FDA Statistical Analysis Plan Guidance

attributes.name: endpoint_description
attributes.description: Full narrative description of the statistical endpoint as stated in the SAP, including the precise definition of the outcome measure, population, and timeframe.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Endpoints; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials

attributes.name: endpoint_name
attributes.description: Short, human-readable name of the statistical endpoint as defined in the SAP (e.g., 'Overall Survival', 'Change from Baseline in HbA1c at Week 24'). Used in TLF titles and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC ADaM; FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Endpoints

attributes.name: endpoint_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the statistical endpoint definition within the SAP authoring and versioning workflow: draft (being authored), under_review (in statistical/medical review), approved (finalized in SAP), locked (post-database lock, immutable), superseded (replaced by a newer version), or retired (no longer active).
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Analysis Plan Guidance; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: endpoint_type
attributes.description: Scientific domain classification of the endpoint: efficacy (clinical benefit), pharmacokinetic (PK - drug exposure), pharmacodynamic (PD - drug effect), biomarker (biological marker), patient_reported_outcome (PRO - patient self-report), or safety. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: efficacy|pharmacokinetic|pharmacodynamic|biomarker|patient_reported_outcome|safety — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC ADaM; FDA Guidance on Biomarker Qualification; EMA PRO Guidance

attributes.name: hypothesis_type
attributes.description: Type of statistical hypothesis being tested for this endpoint: superiority (treatment better than control), non-inferiority (treatment not worse by a defined margin), equivalence (treatment within bounds of control), or exploratory (no formal hypothesis). Drives regulatory interpretation of results.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Non-Inferiority Clinical Trials; EMA Guideline on Non-Inferiority

attributes.name: interim_analysis_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this endpoint is included in one or more pre-specified interim analyses (e.g., for Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) review or adaptive design decision rules). True if the endpoint is evaluated at interim; False if final analysis only.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs; DSMB Charter

attributes.name: locked_date
attributes.description: Date on which this endpoint definition was locked following database lock (DBL), rendering it immutable for regulatory submission purposes. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Analysis Plan Guidance; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: measurement_scale
attributes.description: Statistical measurement scale of the endpoint variable: continuous (numeric), binary (two outcomes), categorical (nominal groups), ordinal (ranked categories), or time_to_event (survival/event-time). Determines the appropriate statistical test method.
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC ADaM; FDA Statistical Guidance on Reporting for Clinical Trials

attributes.name: missing_data_method
attributes.description: Pre-specified method for handling missing data for this endpoint (e.g., 'Multiple Imputation', 'Last Observation Carried Forward (LOCF)', 'Baseline Observation Carried Forward (BOCF)', 'Mixed Model for Repeated Measures (MMRM)', 'Complete Case Analysis'). Defined in the SAP per ICH E9(R1). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: multiple_imputation|locf|bocf|mmrm|complete_case|worst_case — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands; FDA Guidance on Missing Data; EMA Guideline on Missing Data

attributes.name: multiplicity_adjustment_method
attributes.description: Statistical method applied to control the family-wise error rate (FWER) or false discovery rate (FDR) when testing multiple endpoints: Bonferroni, Hochberg, Holm, Benjamini-Hochberg, fixed-sequence, gatekeeping, or none. Required for regulatory submissions with multiple primary or secondary endpoints. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: bonferroni|hochberg|holm|benjamini_hochberg|fixed_sequence|gatekeeping|none — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Multiple Endpoints; EMA Guideline on Multiplicity Issues

attributes.name: multiplicity_testing_family
attributes.description: Name or label of the multiplicity testing family or hierarchy to which this endpoint belongs (e.g., 'Primary Family', 'Secondary Family 1'). Used to group endpoints within a gatekeeping or hierarchical testing procedure defined in the SAP.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Multiple Endpoints; EMA Guideline on Multiplicity Issues

attributes.name: non_inferiority_margin
attributes.description: Pre-specified non-inferiority margin (delta) for non-inferiority or equivalence endpoints, representing the largest clinically acceptable difference between treatment and control. Required by FDA and EMA for non-inferiority trial designs.
attributes.references: FDA Guidance on Non-Inferiority Clinical Trials; EMA Guideline on Non-Inferiority; ICH E9

attributes.name: null_hypothesis
attributes.description: Formal statement of the null hypothesis (H0) for this endpoint as specified in the SAP (e.g., 'There is no difference in overall survival between treatment and control arms'). Required for confirmatory endpoints per ICH E9.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials; FDA Statistical Analysis Plan Guidance

attributes.name: regulatory_designation
attributes.description: Regulatory authority-specific designation of this endpoint indicating its role in submissions to FDA, EMA, or both. attributes.references: FDA IND/NDA/BLA Guidance; EMA MAA Guidance; ICH E9; ICH CTD

attributes.name: sap_version

attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Analysis Plan Guidance; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

attributes.name: sensitivity_analysis_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether one or more pre-specified sensitivity analyses are defined for this endpoint in the SAP to assess the robustness of the primary analysis results. True if sensitivity analyses are planned; False otherwise.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands; FDA Guidance on Missing Data; EMA Guideline on Missing Data

attributes.name: significance_level
attributes.description: Pre-specified Type I error rate (alpha) for this endpoint, typically 0.05 for primary endpoints or adjusted values for multiplicity-controlled secondary endpoints. Defined in the SAP prior to database lock.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance; EMA Guideline on Multiplicity Issues in Clinical Trials

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this endpoint definition was sourced or managed (e.g., SAS Drug Development for SAP authoring, Veeva Vault for document management). Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.

attributes.name: statistical_test_method
attributes.description: The primary statistical test or model used to analyze this endpoint (e.g., 'ANCOVA', 'Log-rank test', 'Cox proportional hazards model', 'Mixed Model for Repeated Measures (MMRM)', 'Wilcoxon rank-sum test'). attributes.name: subgroup_analysis_flag

attributes.name: testing_sequence_order
attributes.description: Numeric position of this endpoint within the pre-specified hierarchical or fixed-sequence testing procedure. Determines the order in which endpoints are tested to control Type I error. Lower values are tested first.

attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.2; FDA Estimand Framework Guidance

attributes.name: intercurrent_event_strategy
attributes.description: The primary strategy applied to handle intercurrent events (ICEs) for this estimand, per ICH E9(R1) Section 3.2. Defines how post-ICE data are treated in the analysis (e.g., treatment policy ignores ICE occurrence; hypothetical posits ICE did not occur).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.2 — Strategies for Handling Intercurrent Events; EMA Reflection Paper on Estimands

attributes.name: interim_analysis_flag
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this estimand is evaluated at one or more pre-specified interim analyses (e.g., for DSMB/DMC review, adaptive design decision points, or early stopping rules).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; DSMB Charter; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: is_confirmatory
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this estimand is part of the confirmatory (inferential) testing hierarchy, as opposed to exploratory or descriptive analyses. Confirmatory estimands are subject to multiplicity control procedures defined in the SAP.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E9 Statistical Principles; FDA Multiple Endpoints Guidance

attributes.name: is_primary_endpoint
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this estimand corresponds to the study's primary endpoint. Primary endpoint estimands carry the highest regulatory weight and drive sample size calculations and confirmatory testing procedures.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials; FDA Guidance for Industry

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Short human-readable label or title for the estimand (e.g., 'Primary Efficacy Estimand', 'Key Secondary Estimand 1'). Used in TLF headers, CSR statistical sections, and regulatory submission narratives.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); EMA Guideline on the Investigation of Subgroups in Confirmatory Clinical Trials

attributes.name: missing_data_strategy
attributes.description: The statistical strategy applied to handle missing outcome data for this estimand (e.g., Last Observation Carried Forward (LOCF), multiple imputation, mixed model for repeated measures). Distinct from the ICE strategy — addresses data gaps rather than post-ICE observations.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); NRC Panel on Handling Missing Data in Clinical Trials; FDA Guidance on Missing Data

attributes.name: multiplicity_adjustment_method
attributes.description: The statistical method used to control Type I error across multiple estimands or endpoints in the confirmatory testing hierarchy (e.g., 'Bonferroni', 'Hochberg', 'Hierarchical testing', 'Gatekeeping procedure'). Null if estimand is exploratory.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Multiple Endpoints in Clinical Trials; EMA Guideline on Multiplicity Issues

attributes.name: non_inferiority_margin
attributes.description: The pre-specified non-inferiority margin (delta) for this estimand, applicable when the effect direction is non-inferiority. Expressed in the units of the summary measure. Null for superiority or equivalence estimands.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Non-Inferiority Clinical Trials; EMA Guideline on the Choice of the Non-Inferiority Margin

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional biostatistician commentary, regulatory discussion points, or cross-references not captured in structured fields. Supports regulatory submission narrative preparation and internal review discussions.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E3 CSR Structure

attributes.name: population_level_summary
attributes.description: The 'Summary Measure' component of the ICH E9(R1) estimand framework — the statistical measure used to summarize the endpoint at the population level (e.g., 'Difference in means', 'Odds ratio', 'Hazard ratio', 'Difference in proportions').
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.1 — Summary Measure; CDISC ADaM; ICH E9 Statistical Principles

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: The primary regulatory framework or agency guideline under which this estimand is defined and will be submitted. Determines the specific regulatory expectations for estimand documentation in the Clinical Study Report (CSR). attributes.name: sap_section_reference

attributes.name: sensitivity_analysis_description

attributes.name: is_stratified_by_site

attributes.description: Indicates whether variable (random) block sizes are used rather than a fixed block size. Variable blocks reduce the ability to predict upcoming assignments and are preferred for double-blind studies.
